findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "connection_route" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Work out which ENA connection procedure a domestic installation of solar panels, batteries or both falls under: connect first and notify the distribution networ…

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_documents" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search the guides, articles and questions for material on a UK home energy subject. Use this first, before answering from memory, whenever a question concerns U…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_document · Private data: connection_route, get_document, heat_pump_noise, list_documents, search_documents, solar_pv_shading · Public sink: connection_route · Destructive: heat_pump_running_cost, heat_pump_size, radiator_flow_temperature, room_heat_loss.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_document · Private data: connection_route, get_document, heat_pump_noise, list_documents, search_documents, solar_pv_shading · Public sink: connection_route · Destructive: heat_pump_running_cost, heat_pump_size, radiator_flow_temperature, room_heat_loss

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
